hypotheses: SMER-3 at 10 uM for 24 h in A375 produces a histone-mark profile with strong depletion of H3K27me0K36me2 and related H3K27me1/K36me2 states, and relative enrichment of H3K27me3K36me1.
Donors with high anchor similarity to this A375 profile are more likely to transfer a reproducible histone perturbation in the target context.

Roscovitine, KU-55933, etoposide, resveratrol, and momelotinib are prioritized because their measured anchor similarities are among the highest available and span distinct pharmacological classes, allowing comparison of chromatin-associated versus DNA-damage/kinase-related mechanisms.

The fixed decoder will transfer donor target-minus-A375 responses and select one target cell/feature/sign; the selected donor should yield a histone perturbation exceeding 0.5 log2 versus vehicle without implying viability or causality.
object.evidence_gap: No direct histone-mark response values are provided for SMER-3 or the candidate donors in the target context; donor selection relies on anchor similarity and pharmacology descriptions, and the actual transferred target-cell feature/sign must be determined by the fixed external decoder.
